evidence.V1: Doorway hole reads in the silhouette and front; the 3/4 reads as a walk-through door wall from every angle.
evidence.V2: Big wall slab, medium jamb stones / lintel course / door frame, small gold keystone - clear three tiers.
evidence.V3: Wall and jambs are good chunky stylised stone, but the doorway is a tall plain rectangle with a very thin uniform trim frame; reads somewhat stiff/primitive.
evidence.V4: Stones and cap have consistent chamfers that catch light, but the gold keystone is an unbevelled razor-edged trapezoid (lintel_studio/flat) and the frame bevel is very small, so treatment is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Doorway, lintel and end-section close-ups are clean; no pinches, seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone in three values plus a gold keystone accent; brick/slate colourways keep the structure.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, stone hue with gold keystone as specified for the modular kit, chamfered blocks.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default (keeps doorway walkable), CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling pass (iou 0.99).

artifacts: Keystone has no chamfer, reads razor-sharp against the bevelled stones
top_fixes: Chamfer the keystone and enlarge it slightly (or make it a real voussoir in the lintel course) so it reads at 64 px
Give the door frame more depth/width or replace it with stone jamb blocks + a proper lintel so the opening is less of a plain rectangle
Consider a slightly arched or stepped head to add stylised character
